mercy_translation.text:
Whoever comes and teaches you all the things said above, receive him. But if the teacher himself turns aside and teaches another teaching so as to destroy this one, do not listen to him. If, however, he teaches so as to increase righteousness and knowledge of the Lord, receive him as the Lord.

Concerning apostles and prophets, act according to the ordinance of the Gospel. Let every apostle who comes to you be received as the Lord. He shall remain for one day; if there is need, also the next. But if he remains three days, he is a false prophet.

When the apostle departs, let him take nothing except enough bread to reach his next lodging. If he asks for money, he is a false prophet.

Do not test or judge any prophet who speaks in the Spirit; for every sin will be forgiven, but this sin will not be forgiven. Yet not everyone who speaks in the Spirit is a prophet, but only the one who has the ways of the Lord. Therefore the false prophet and the true prophet will be known by their conduct.

No prophet who, in the Spirit, orders a meal shall eat from it; otherwise he is a false prophet. Every prophet who teaches the truth but does not practice what he teaches is a false prophet.

But every prophet who has been tested and found true, acting for the earthly mystery of the Church yet not teaching others to do everything he himself does, shall not be judged by you; his judgment is with God. The ancient prophets acted in the same way.

If anyone says in the Spirit, "Give me money," or anything else, do not listen to him. But if he tells you to give for others who are in need, let no one judge him.

translator_notes: Direct Mercy translation from the Greek public-domain source.
The chapter gives criteria for discerning itinerant apostles and prophets.
The difficult phrase μυστήριον κοσμικὸν ἐκκλησίας is rendered cautiously as 'the earthly mystery of the Church' and should remain flagged for further philological review.
